items.title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
items.abstract: The context lengths of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly increasing in real-world applications such as agentic systems and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). To accelerate LLM inference in these scenarios, reusing position-independent key-value (KV) caches across requests has emerged as a promising approach. This technique typically relies on recomputing a selected subset of tokens to restore cross-chunk interactions. However, existing solutions suffer from critical limitations in both algorithmic efficiency and system deployment. Algorithmically, they overlook the distribution of KV

items.what: Position-independent caching을 분산 클러스터에서 구현하고, prefill completion time을 통신·계산 비용으로 모델링하여 스케줄링 최적화
items.relation: prefill 최적화와 클러스터 통신을 동시에 다루며, H1(통신 vs 계산)과 H2(병렬화 전략)의 핵심 관찰을 공유
items.gap: GPU 대규모 분산 시스템 가정. 우리는 CPU-only, 1GbE, 소규모 클러스터로 전제가 상이하며, 메모리 용량 확장보다 단일 노드 계산 효율이 핵심
hypothesis_notes: H1: prefill 시간의 25~45 %가 통신+barrier 대기이며, 그중 대기(straggler) 가 순수 전송보다 크다
H2: S ≤ 4K 구간에서는 attention의 O(S²) 항이 지배적이지 않고 MLP/projection이 병목

items.title: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference

We therefore introduce TriAttention, which assigns query-key (QK) tiles to skipping, 4-bit, or 8-bit computation, using 4-bit to retain quantization-tolerant interactions at lower cost. all.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
all.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. all.abstract: Agent applications are evolving into workflows composed of large language model (LLM) calls and tool invocations, termed modules. Existing distributed agent systems typically adopt a disaggregated architecture, deploying different modules on separate devices. While this enables pipeline parallelism, imbalanced module latencies introduce severe pipeline bubbles that limit throughput. all.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
all.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur severe memory-access overheads due to the cost of loading large weight matrices and key-value (KV) caches. Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) is an emerging solution that enables computation directly on static weights stored in memory, substantially reducing energy and latency. 3D-IMC further stacks memory arrays into vertical tiers, increasing capacity but revealing a new challenge: how weights are placed in memory determines which matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) can execute concurrently, affecting latency and throughput. all.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
all.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents' precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. all.relation: 학습 절차의 mismatch를 다루며, 우리는 inference(prefill) 시간 최적화로 도메인이 완전히 다름
all.gap: 우리는 inference의 계산 최적화이고, 이 논문은 training 절차의 정확도 문제로 별개의 문제
all.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
all.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own responses, guided by a fixed teacher. Generating these responses is expensive, so systems use quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts to reduce the cost. Both, however, introduce training-inference mismatch between the rollout engine and the model being trained. Such mismatch can destabilize reinforcement learning (RL), but its effects on OPD remain unclear. This paper investigates how much mismatch OPD tolerates, where its effects arise, and how training systems can use this tolerance. Measuring all mismatch sources
